item.text:
**Bottom Line**  
Mixed, leaning slightly positive on acute disaster relief and some displacement management, but weak on protection from violence and on showing transparent, evidence-led correction beyond official tallies.

**Accepted Claims**
- `Autoridades de los tres órdenes de gobierno coordinan acciones de apoyo en Guerrero y Oaxaca ante los efectos del huracán John` | Secretaría de Seguridad y Protección Ciudadana | 2024-09-24 | https://www.gob.mx/sspc/prensa/autoridades-de-los-tres-ordenes-de-gobierno-coordinan-acciones-de-apoyo-en-guerrero-y-oaxaca-ante-los-efectos-del-huracan-john | The federal response to Hurricane John was tracked through concrete metrics: early-warning bulletins, a large joint response force, evacuation support, and work to restore electricity, water, and transport. This is strong evidence of active crisis mitigation. | IDs: 6B.6, 6B.5
- `25 mil elementos de Fuerzas Armadas y Guardia Nacional auxilian a población de Guerrero por tormenta tropical John` | Presidencia de México | 2024-09-27 | https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/25-mil-elementos-de-fuerzas-armadas-y-guardia-nacional-auxilian-a-poblacion-de-guerrero-por-tormenta-tropical-john/ | AMLO said roughly 25,000 personnel were deployed, shelters were active, and the priority was saving lives during the storm. That supports the view that the government tried to reduce avoidable disaster suffering quickly. | IDs: 6B.6, 6B.5
- `13ª Reunión del Puesto de Comando en seguimiento sobre las acciones implementadas en Acapulco, Guerrero` | Secretaría de Seguridad y Protección Ciudadana | 2024-10-03 | https://www.gob.mx/sspc/prensa/13-reunion-del-puesto-de-comando-en-seguimiento-sobre-las-acciones-implementadas-en-acapulco-guerrero | The recovery effort after John was still being measured in operational terms: 99 shelters, 8,999 people housed, 5,237 medical attentions, and thousands of food rations delivered. This is direct evidence of coordinated emergency service delivery. | IDs: 6B.6, 6B.5
- `Gobierno federal reporta acciones de apoyo a Acapulco y Coyuca de Benítez por huracán Otis; prevención es fundamental: presidente` | Presidencia de México | 2024-06-17 | https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/gobierno-federal-reporta-acciones-de-apoyo-a-acapulco-y-coyuca-de-benitez-por-huracan-otis-prevencion-es-fundamental-presidente/ | The government framed Otis recovery around continuing, coordinated reconstruction and repeatedly cited service-restoration and support for affected people. This is useful evidence that disaster response remained an ongoing priority rather than a one-off gesture. | IDs: 6B.6, 6B.5
- `Continúa atención a damnificados por huracán Otis: presidente; evalúa IMSS Bienestar` | Presidencia de México | 2024-03-16 | https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/continua-atencion-a-damnificados-por-huracan-otis-presidente-evalua-imss-bienestar/ | AMLO said 300,000 families had been helped after Otis and linked the recovery tour to health-system evaluation. That suggests the administration was trying to combine disaster relief with service restoration. | IDs: 6B.6, 6B.2, 6B.5
- `Abasto de agua en el país está garantizado; no se otorgan concesiones a industrias de alto consumo: presidente` | Presidencia de México | 2024-04-19 | https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/abasto-de-agua-en-el-pais-esta-garantizado-no-se-otorgan-concesiones-a-industrias-de-alto-consumo-presidente/ | AMLO said domestic water use would be prioritized and that the government was drilling new wells and addressing drought. That is direct evidence of crisis-oriented management of a basic necessity under scarcity pressure. | IDs: 6B.6, 6B.2
- `Biden y AMLO agreed to coordinate immediate measures to reduce irregular border crossings while protecting human rights` | Reuters | 2024-04-30 | https://theprint.in/world/us-mexico-to-clamp-down-on-illegal-immigration-leaders-say/2062785/ | The migration response was handled through bilateral coordination and explicit human-rights language rather than blanket coercion. This is limited but real evidence of trying to reduce suffering in a displacement-related crisis. | IDs: 6B.6, 6B.3
- `Rampant extortion reveals corrosive hole in Mexico security strategy` | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-01-25 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/rampant-extortion-reveals-corrosive-hole-in-mexico-security-strategy-3283251 | Reuters reported extortion remained far above the level when AMLO took office. That undercuts any strong claim that everyday crisis suffering from criminal coercion was materially reduced. | IDs: 6B.6, 6B.1
- `Mexico: Killings of journalists show need to strengthen federal protection mechanism` | Amnesty International / CPJ | 2024-03-06 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/03/mexico-killings-journalists-strengthen-federal-mechanism/ | Amnesty said journalists enrolled in the federal protection mechanism were still being killed. That is direct negative evidence that the state was not effectively reducing avoidable suffering for a high-risk group during an ongoing protection crisis. | IDs: 6B.6, 6B.3
- `Mexican soldiers killed six migrants` | Reuters | 2024-10-16 | https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/mexico-militarys-role-in-migrant-massacre-comes-under-sharp-scrutiny-2024-10-16/ | Reuters reported soldiers killed six migrants, with the military account disputed locally. This is strong negative evidence that vulnerable people remained exposed to lethal harm during a displacement-related crisis. | IDs: 6B.6, 6B.3
- `Mexico | World Report 2024` | Human Rights Watch | 2024 | https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/mexico | HRW said AMLO made little progress on extreme criminal violence, abuses against migrants, gender-based violence, attacks on journalists and defenders, torture, disappearances, and extrajudicial killings. This is broad counterevidence that avoidable suffering was not brought under control. | IDs: 6B.6, 6B.3
- `Visita a México: informe del Grupo de Trabajo sobre la Detención Arbitraria` | ONU-DH / UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention | 2024-09-17 | https://hchr.org.mx/relatorias_grupos/visita-a-mexico-informe-del-grupo-de-trabajo-sobre-la-detencion-arbitraria/ | The UN Working Group said arbitrary detention remained widespread and that military/navy detentions were not always entered in the registry. That is negative evidence of unresolved avoidable suffering tied to coercive state practice. | IDs: 6B.6, 6B.5, 6B.3
- `Mexico’s central bank cuts benchmark interest rate to 10.75% in divided vote` | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-08-08 | https://www.investing.com/news/commodities-news/mexicos-central-bank-cuts-benchmark-interest-rate-to-1075-in-divided-vote-3562752 | Banxico was easing only as inflation slowed, but Reuters still noted inflation remained elevated. This is mixed evidence: the macro framework was functioning, but price-pressure suffering was not cleanly resolved. | IDs: 6B.6, 6B.5
- `Mexico’s GDP, inflation figures support bets of September rate cut` | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-08-22 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/mexicos-gdp-inflation-figures-support-bets-of-september-rate-cut-3583901 | Slower inflation allowed further easing, but growth remained tepid. That suggests partial stabilization, not a decisive reduction of economic-shock suffering. | IDs: 6B.6, 6B.5

**Search Gap**
- The strongest positive evidence is official and operational: government and SSPC reports give detailed response counts for hurricanes, water scarcity, and migration coordination.
- I did not find much independent 2024 after-action evaluation showing whether AMLO’s crisis responses measurably lowered deaths, displacement, or hardship over time.
- On the negative side, independent reporting remains strong on unresolved violence, migrant abuse, and extortion, so the record is not one of broad crisis success.
